text.p: Britain's Ladbroke Group Plc confirmed on Monday that it had concluded a long-awaited global deal with Hilton Hotels Corp of the U.S that will deepen the two firms' existing marketing cooperation and pave the way for full cross-shareholding investments.
Having signed the agreements, first anounced last summer, the pair said in a statement they would implement the first major initiative, a global loyalty programme, on February 1.
Hilton Hotels Corp owns the Hilton name within the U.S., while Ladbroke's Hilton International unit holds the rights to the name elsewhere in the world.

In essence the cooperation deal will reunite the Hilton brand across the world after 32 years, the firms said in a statement, adding, "The signing of the legal agreements paves the way for a rapid implementation of the key features of the alliance."

With 400 hotels spanning 49 countries, the Hilton HHonors Worldwide (rpt HHonors) loyalty programme is intended to "further enhance Hilton's leadership position in one of the world's fastest-growing industries".
As expected, the agreements signed confirm that the pair will be able to take cross shareholdings and that HHC intends to acquire a 5.0 percent stake in Ladbroke in due course.
